title: What Can Travel Through Remotes
summary: Remote arguments are serialized: numbers, strings, booleans, tables (copied!), Instances (as references the receiver must reach), and engine datatypes pass; functions, metatables, and threads don't. Size limits apply.

explanation.whatItIs: The packing rules for the remote pipeline: flat data + tables + instance references in; impossible types rejected.
explanation.whyItExists: The network moves bytes; serialization defines which Luau shapes become bytes — and copies instead of sharing.
whenToUse: Instance references when the receiver can reach the same object (replicated content)
IDs instead of objects when the object might not exist for the receiver
whenNotToUse: Enormous payloads every frame — batch and throttle
tips: Receivers get COPIES of tables — mutations don't sync back
Instance args arrive as nil if the object isn't replicated to the receiver
Server always re-validates types — clients can send garbage
commonMistakes: Sending an unreplicated Instance to a client → nil
Assuming shared table state across the boundary
Exceeding size limits with giant serialized blobs

examples.title: Do and don't
examples.code:
-- ✅ Fine:
remote:FireServer(10, "sword", { level = 3 }, Vector3.new(0, 5, 0))
remote:FireServer(workspace.ReplicatedModels.SwordTemplate)  -- replicated instance

-- ❌ Errors:
-- remote:FireServer(function() end)   -- functions can't serialize
-- remote:FireServer(coroutine.running())  -- threads can't either

-- ⚠️ Copies:
local data = { coins = 5 }
remote:FireServer(data)
data.coins = 999   -- receiver still saw 5
